Hi all,

I pulled the account history and ran it through our promo-abuse signals. Short summary:
- Four promo credit requests in the last 30 days across three distinct email aliases (elena.morales@, elena.morales+dev@, elena.morales.ds@) all tied to the same billing card and shipping address.
- IPs associated with signups cluster in two CIDR ranges that have previously been used by known trial-farming patterns (internal tag: TF-94).
- Usage spike on 2026-11-12 appears to be synthetic token churn: many short-lived sessions with similar prompt lengths and repeated prefixes.
- No SSO/enterprise domain verification on file; primary contact is a generic gmail/forwarding setup for backups.

I’ve attached the raw hits and signup headers for reference (audit_hits_11-20.csv, signup_headers_11-18.txt). Risk assessment: Medium-High for promo abuse. Recommended actions:
1) Put the requested credit on hold pending org verification (corporate email or billing verification).
2) Offer a small conditional credit (e.g., $250) for verified corporate users to keep PoC momentum.
3) If they require the full $2k, require billing verification and a short paid pilot contract first.

If you want, I can draft the verification wording for outreach.

-Neha
Fraud & Risk Analyst
Redwood Inference

Attachments: audit_hits_11-20.csv, signup_headers_11-18.txt
